items.title: [The Marginalian] Wendell Berry on Where Our Loved Ones Gone Go
items.content_html: To love is to sign a contract with loss. To love anyway is both the great tragedy and the great triumph of life. When two people have loved one another, each has become embedded in the marrow of the other’s being and both have had a profound experience that cannot be unhad even when the slender thread of grace between them is severed, by death or disenchantment. “No one you love is ever dead,” Hemingway wrote in his moving meditation on death and the meaning of life disguised as a letter of consolation to a bereaved friend. Death, of course,… read article

items.title: [The Marginalian] Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, and with Fangs: The Alchemy of Unrequited Love and the Story Behind Emily Dickinson’s Most Famous Poem
items.content_html: This essay is adapted from the nineteenth chapter of my book Figuring. In the first autumn of her thirties, Emily Dickinson wrote to her confidante and eventual editor Thomas Wentworth Higginson: I had a terror — since September — I could tell to none, and so I sing, as the Boy does by the Burying Ground — because I am afraid. Not a “fright,” not a “shock,” but a terror. What lay behind this enormity implied by a woman who measured her words so meticulously? Generations of biographers have filled pages with conjectures of varying persuasiveness — a death, some… read article

items.content_html:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority

The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.

Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.

The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The UN has said the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.

items.title: [rapporteur.com] Europe rejects US-Russia security deal without its participation
items.content_html: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 5 that a prospective agreement with Russia to end the war in Ukraine could cover “all of Europe,” after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House. Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner said Washington was developing a wider European security framework but did not provide a full negotiating text. US-mediated talks among Ukraine, Russia and the United States are scheduled for Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi without the European Union at the table. European officials rejected any arrangement on the continent’s security made without their involvement. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said NATO and the EU already have defined roles and Ukraine should be integrated into that framework. She said EU participation is necessary to implement any settlement, including provisions on sanctions, reconstruction and Ukraine’s EU accession. Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said an agreement on Ukraine and Europe made without their involvement would be impossible, while Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha rejected Russia as a guarantor of European security. Europe is also divided over who should represent it. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni urged EU leaders to agree on a representative and mandate by year-end; European Council President António Costa backed a unified EU message. Leaders are due to discuss the representative’s profile and mandate at an informal summit in Dublin on Nov. 13, with a decision sought at the December European Council.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] ‘Every day, someone loses a hand or a leg’: the brutal reality of India’s textile recycling industry
items.content_html:
In Panipat, 1m tons of used clothing a year are turned into products for global brands, but dangerous machinery and few safeguards mean life-changing injuries are common

For three months, Suraj Kumar’s job was to feed discarded clothes into shredding machines in Panipat, an industrial city in the north Indian state of Haryana. Clothes discarded in the US, Canada and Europe arrive in the city to be torn back into fibres and spun into yarn, feeding a textile recycling industry that supplies markets across the world.

Suraj, 19, had travelled from West Bengal state to work in Panipat’s factories, following his cousins and friends who had already found jobs there. items.title: [apnews.com] Paraguay president submits resignation as Ueno collapse freezes millions of accounts
items.content_html: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Nov. 5 as the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank froze access to accounts held by nearly 3 million customers. Minutes later, the Chamber of Deputies voted 78-0 to impeach him. Congress had not accepted the resignation by Friday, Nov. 6, leaving Peña formally in office. He said he would appear at the Senate proceedings to defend himself. Vice President Pedro Alliana is next in line if lawmakers accept Peña’s resignation or remove him through impeachment. Paraguay’s central bank took control of Ueno on Nov. 3 after finding that its solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum. The intervention shut down the bank’s app, cards and transfers. Ueno had about 3 million customers and administered roughly $850 million in public funds, including pension-related money. Lawmakers accuse Peña of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and shielding the bank from scrutiny. He has denied wrongdoing and said the matter should be handled through the courts. Prosecutors ordered three investigations into the bank’s failure, covering oversight, the handling of its collapse and the placement of public funds.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Can an African feminist have a white wedding? It’s complicated | Patience Akumu
items.content_html:
I wanted to be a beacon of black feminist love; my friends and family teased me for being a sellout

We had been together 20 years, had two children and had a customary marriage with our village sub-county two years ago without any real plans for a church wedding. So we called our second ceremony a celebration of love and not a wedding. How else would a self-professed African feminist survive being the centre of a colonial and Abrahamic religious ceremony that also manages to reinforce the most male-centred aspects of African culture?

Our invitations came directly from me and my partner Mark, not – as is traditional – from our families, and in the form of a playful gif featuring the song Love Potion from the South African group Mafikizolo, a reminder that this was a wedding on our terms. I thought they screamed “liberated African feminist”. But when my cousin Moses received his, he asked, “So, the patriarchy has won?”

Carney said U.S. negotiators had dropped objections involving language, culture and Canada’s ability to make trade deals with other countries. He did not identify the major unresolved issues. Trump told Fox News a deal was imminent. Formal negotiations broke down in August as the countries tried to reach a deal before new U.S. tariffs on nearly $28 billion of Canadian goods took effect. Autos remain a sticking point, and Carney did not say when Canada’s chief negotiator would return to Washington. He said formal meetings there were not necessary to keep discussions moving. Carney is due to meet Trump in China later this month.
